title: kbmon shows a landed item as still landing at step verify, because a verify row in the same millisecond as land.end re-adds the landing
goal: A landing whose land.end row is recorded is not shown as in progress by kbmon's sprint panel, even when a land.step row of the item shares its timestamp and follows it; a land.step row with a later timestamp than the land.end row starts a new landing, which still shows

_m=tempfile.mkdtemp

 d=_m(*a,**k);atexit.register(shutil.rmtree,d,True);return d
tempfile.mkdtemp=_d
import os, sys, tempfile
from types import SimpleNamespace
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA"] = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.environ["CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT"] = os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import bl_stall, mon_sprint
T = "2026-11-08T16:48:46.898Z"
def row(i, ev, ts, **kw):
    return {"id": f"{i}", "ts": ts, "event": ev, **kw}
rows = [row(1, "land.step", "2026-11-08T16:40:00.000Z", item="ST-aaaaaaaa", step="rebase"),
        row(2, "land.step", "2026-11-08T16:44:00.000Z", item="ST-aaaaaaaa", step="verify"),
        row(3, "land.end", T, item="ST-aaaaaaaa", exit=0),
        row(4, "land.step", T, item="ST-aaaaaaaa", step="verify"),
        row(5, "land.step", "2026-11-08T16:41:00.000Z", item="ST-bbbbbbbb", step="verify"),
        row(6, "land.end", "2026-11-08T16:42:00.000Z", item="ST-bbbbbbbb", exit=1),
        row(7, "land.step", "2026-11-08T16:50:00.000Z", item="ST-bbbbbbbb", step="rebase")]
bl = SimpleNamespace(items={i: {"status": "doing", "title": f"Title {i}"} for i in ("ST-aaaaaaaa", "ST-bbbbbbbb")})
bl_stall.ops_rows = lambda root: list(rows)
found = {x["item"]: x["step"] for x in mon_sprint.landings(tempfile.mkdtemp(), bl)}
print(found)
sys.exit(not not found != {"ST-bbbbbbbb": "rebase"})

gates.question: How does the landings reader tell a late land.step from a retry's?
options: Compare the step row's ts with its item's last land.end ts: at or before it is late, later starts a landing, whatever the end's exit
Ignore a step after a land.end of exit 0 whatever its ts, as the sessions panel does
gates.recommendation: Compare the step row's ts with its item's last land.end ts: at or before it is late, later starts a landing, whatever the end's exit
gates.answer: Compare the step row's ts with its item's last land.end ts: at or before it is late, later starts a landing, whatever the end's exit

notes: Evidence 2026-11-08: --status sprints printed 'landing A paid session-load record..., at step verify, last step 29 min ago' and 'landing Sessions no person watches..., at step verify, last step 11.2 days ago' while ops showed land.end exit=0 at 16:48:46.898Z and backlog.py runs said landed; mon_sprint's landing reader (landings) removes the landing on land.end and the trailing verify row adds it back. Relates to BG-v53lnj6a and BG-i6vjrbng (row order of land.end and land.step). Premise run 2026-11-08: the repro PASSES (exit 0), because no live landing is at step verify now: the two it was filed on are gone from the panel, so it proves nothing and is kept only as the filed command. Planted check 0 (bl_stall.ops_rows replaced by planted rows, mon_sprint.landings on a planted backlog object, in an isolated query-log home) fails on the base: ST-aaaaaaaa shows at step verify after its land.end of the same millisecond. The reading of a later-timestamp land.step as a new landing is settled in the goal, so a failed landing's retry still shows.
